title: How a Network Learns
eyebrow: CETI · feature · a two-layer network learning Fisher's irises · draft B, the night garden
lede: A small network learns 150 irises. The loss falls off a wall in a few dozen steps; the last few flowers cost hundreds. Flowers as a cloud in the dark, the loss surface rising out of the ground, the signal pulsing through the ribbons, the right ones lit like dawn.

chapters.title: Fast at first

captions: A small network is shown 150 flowers and their names.
After 10 steps of learning, how many does it get right?
Irises measured by Edgar Anderson in 1935; Fisher, 1936.
150 flowers, 3 species, 4 measurements. Three drawn here.
Setosa stands apart: no petal longer than 1.9 cm.
Versicolor and virginica overlap: 37 share 4.5–5.1 cm.
The network: 4 measurements in, 8 hidden units, 3 names out.
67 weights decide its answers. Wrong answers cost loss.
Two of the weights as ground, loss as height.
Learning is 1,000 steps downhill. It starts at loss 1.393.
Off the wall at once, then a long crawl down to 0.039.
The same 150 flowers ride through the network.
Random weights: 13 land on the right name.
After 10 steps: 135 right. 122 more, in 10 steps.
Step 50: 144. Step 100: 146. The weights keep growing.
Step 1,000: 148 of 150. 2 never land right.
Lit = right. 90 % of the loss drop is done by step 34.
From 13 to 140 right took 23 steps. The last 8 took 208.
Then 769 more steps, and not one more flower.
The 2 it misses sit where versicolor and virginica overlap.
Monday: when the curve goes flat, what is it still missing?
Graded on the 150 it learned from; new flowers untested.

brand.takeaway: Fast at first. The last few cost the most.

Anderson E. The irises of the Gaspé Peninsula. Bulletin of the American Iris Society 1935;59:2–5.
Fisher RA. Iris [dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository, 1988. doi:10.24432/C56C76. With Bezdek JC et al. Will the real iris data please stand up? IEEE Trans Fuzzy Systems 1999;7(3):368–369.

Rumelhart DE, Hinton GE, Williams RJ. Learning representations by back-propagating errors. Nature 1986;323:533–536.
Li H, Xu Z, Taylor G, Studer C, Goldstein T. Visualizing the loss landscape of neural nets. NeurIPS 2018.
honest: Graded on the 150 it learned from; new flowers untested. One tiny network, one learning rate; the landscape is a 2-D slice with the other 65 weights held at step 1,000.
